# A spatial multi-omic portrait of survival outcome for clear cell renal cell carcinoma, Meyer et al., 2026

**DISCLAIMER**: The study is currently undergoing peer-review. Therefore, the code base is under active development. It includes code for all data presented in the manuscript but also exploratory data analysis parts. File paths have to be adjusted by the user. 

# Segmentation Quality Control

masks:
final mask (masks_cp6 = masks) = Ir191, Ir193, H3, SMA, CA9, panCK, CD8a, CD68 (diam 15)

other masks tried:
masks_cp2 = Ir191, Ir193, H3, SMA, Vim, CA9, panCK, CD8a, CD68 (diam 15)
masks_cp5 = Ir191, Ir193, H3, SMA, CA9, panCK, CD8a, CD68 (diam 10)


## Safety check
It is crucial that the order of the images in both CytoImageList objects is the same.
```{r}
all.equal(names(images), names(masks))
```

## Add additional metadata to the `elementMetadata` slot of the `CytoImageList` (accessible via mcols)
```{r}
# Read in images
images_meta <- read_csv("/mnt/central_nas/users/marllu/T_panel/images.csv",col_names = TRUE)
images_meta$names <- str_split(images_meta$image,".tiff",simplify = TRUE)[,1]
images_meta$TMA_id <- str_split(images_meta$acquisition_description," ",simplify = TRUE)[,1]


# Add information to metadata of CytoImageList
mcols(images)$sample_id <- images_meta$names[match(names(images),images_meta$names)] # sample_id is set to image name
mcols(images)$TMA_id <- images_meta$TMA_id[match(names(images),images_meta$names)]


# Read in external metadata
patient_meta <- read_csv("/mnt/central_nas/users/marllu/T_panel/data_analysis/data/Metadata_combined_RCC.csv",col_names = TRUE)
patient_meta$TMA_id <- str_replace(paste0(patient_meta$grid,"x",patient_meta$x,"y",patient_meta$y),"NA","")
patient_meta$TMA_id <- str_replace(patient_meta$TMA_id, "x","X")
patient_meta$TMA_id <- str_replace(patient_meta$TMA_id, "y","Y")


# Add information to metadata of CytoImageList
mcols(images)$PID <- patient_meta$PID[match(mcols(images)$TMA_id,patient_meta$TMA_id)]
mcols(images)$type <- patient_meta$type[match(mcols(images)$TMA_id,patient_meta$TMA_id)]
mcols(images)$subtype <- patient_meta$subtype[match(mcols(images)$TMA_id,patient_meta$TMA_id)]

images_meta$PID <- patient_meta$PID[match(images_meta$TMA_id,patient_meta$TMA_id)]

# Transfer to masks objects as well
mcols(masks) <- mcols(images)
```


# View images

## A: `plotPixels` function from [cytomapper](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/cytomapper.html).

### Plot Images
#### Random images

Here, we select 30 random images and perform image- and channel-wise normalization (channels are first min-max normalized and scaled to a range of 0-1 before clipping the maximum intensity to 0.2).

```{r}
#Randomly select 30 images
# set.seed(202311) # used for first images (without letter)
# set.seed(301123) # used for images "A"
set.seed(1999) # used for images "B" => different markers plotted
set.seed(051223) # used for "D"
set.seed(111223) # used for "G"


i_random <- sample(seq_len(length(images)), 30)

# Normalize and clip image
cur_images <- images[i_random]
cur_images <- cytomapper::normalize(cur_images, separateImages = TRUE)
cur_images <- cytomapper::normalize(cur_images, inputRange = c(0, 0.2))
```

# Dimensionality reduction

## Define interesting channels for Dimensionality reduction

```{r}
rowData(sce)$use_channel_dim <- grepl("SMA|panCK|CD68|CD8|Ca9|CD4|Vim|CD45RO", rowData(sce)$clean_target)

# check
rowData(sce)$clean_target[rowData(sce)$use_channel_dim=="TRUE"] # check which chaannel == "TRUE"
```

## Subset to ccRCC 
```{r}
sce$subtype <- mcols(images)$subtype[match(sce$sample_id, mcols(images)$sample_id)]

sce_ccRCC <- sce[,!is.na(sce$subtype)]
sce_ccRCC <- sce[,sce$subtype == "clear_cell_RCC"]
```

## Run tSNE and UMAP
```{r}
## Subsample 10% of cells from each core
#to save time and not get super crowded dimensionality reduction plots
set.seed(22)

subcp <- colData(sce_ccRCC) %>% as.data.frame() %>% group_by("sample_id") %>% slice_sample(prop = 0.1) %>% arrange("sample_id") %>% mutate(sub_id = paste(sample_id,ObjectNumber,sep="_")) %>% pull(sub_id)
sce_sub <- sce_ccRCC[,subcp]


#Run UMAP/TSNE
# cp
sce_sub <- runUMAP(sce_sub[rowData(sce_sub)$use_channel_dim,], n_neighbors = 30, pca = 50,exprs_values = "exprs", external_neighbors=TRUE, BPPARAM = MulticoreParam())
sce_sub <- runTSNE(sce_sub[rowData(sce_sub)$use_channel_dim,], exprs_values = "exprs", external_neighbors=TRUE, BPPARAM = MulticoreParam())
```

# Image level quality control

## S/N pixel level

It is often of interest to calculate the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for individual channels and markers. Here, we define the SNR as
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
library(EBImage)

cur_snr <- lapply(names(images), function(x){
    img <- images[[x]] 
    mat <- apply(img, 3, function(ch){                                          # the 3rd dimension are the 46 channels
        # Otsu threshold
        thres <- otsu(ch, range = c(min(ch), max(ch)), levels = 65536)
        # Signal-to-noise ratio
        snr <- mean(ch[ch > thres]) / mean(ch[ch <= thres])
        # Signal intensity
        ps <- mean(ch[ch > thres])
        
        return(c(snr = snr, ps = ps))
    })
    
    t(mat) %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
        mutate(image = x,
               marker = colnames(mat)) %>% 
        pivot_longer(cols = c(snr, ps))
})

cur_snr <- do.call(rbind, cur_snr)

cur_snr %>% 
    group_by(marker, name) %>%
    summarize(log_mean = log2(mean(value))) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = log_mean) %>%
    ggplot() +
    geom_point(aes(ps, snr)) +
    geom_label_repel(aes(ps, snr, label = marker), max.overlaps = 50) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 15) + ylab("Signal-to-noise ratio [log2]") +
    xlab("Signal intensity [log2]")
```


Otsu thesholding and SNR calculation does not perform well if the markers are lowly abundant. In the next code chunk, we will remove markers that have a positive signal of below 2 per image.

```{r}
cur_snr <- cur_snr %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = value) %>%
    filter(ps > 2) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(snr, ps))

cur_snr %>% 
    group_by(marker, name) %>%
    summarize(log_mean = log2(mean(value))) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = log_mean) %>%
    ggplot() +
    geom_point(aes(ps, snr)) +
    geom_label_repel(aes(ps, snr, label = marker), max.overlaps = 50) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 15) + ylab("Signal-to-noise ratio [log2]") +
    xlab("Signal intensity [log2]")
```


## Image area covered by cells

Another quality indicator is the image area covered by cells (or biological tissue).

```{r}
cell_density <- colData(sce) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    group_by(sample_id) %>%
    # Compute the number of pixels covered by cells and 
    # the total number of pixels
    summarize(cell_area = sum(area),
              no_pixels = mean(width_px) * mean(height_px)) %>%
    # Divide the total number of pixels 
    # by the number of pixels covered by cells
    mutate(covered_area = cell_area / no_pixels)


# Visualize the image area covered by cells per image
ggplot(cell_density) +
        geom_point(aes(reorder(sample_id,covered_area), covered_area)) + 
        theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 15)) +
        ylim(c(0, 1)) +
        ylab("% covered area") + xlab("")


# look at critical images
cimg <- cell_density$sample_id[cell_density$covered_area<0.1]

# extract TMA_id
mcols(images)$TMA_id[mcols(images)$sample_id %in% cimg]
# look at their segmentation
```

to identify images with outlying marker expression

```{r}
                                   ids = sce$sample_id, 
                                   statistics="mean",

assay(image_mean, "exprs") <- asinh(counts(image_mean))
```
